claim: As triggers, Amazon SQS is pull-based (consumers poll the queue), Amazon SNS is push-based (subscribers receive messages when published), and EventBridge is event-driven (rules match events and route them to targets).
question: How do SQS, SNS and EventBridge differ in how they deliver work to a Lambda function?

values.display: Pull-based (consumers poll messages from the queue)
rules match events and route to targets

qualifiers.scope: Amazon SQS versus Amazon SNS versus Amazon EventBridge

evidence.quote: |  Communication model  |  Pull-based (consumers poll messages from the queue)  |  Push-based (subscribers receive messages when published)  |  Event-driven (rules match events and route to targets)  |

claim: Typical uses: SQS for decoupling microservices, buffering requests and processing tasks asynchronously; SNS for fanout notifications and pub/sub messaging; EventBridge for event-driven architectures, real-time stream processing and cross-account event sharing.
question: Which of SQS, SNS or EventBridge fits buffering, fan-out, or cross-account event routing in front of Lambda?
